body:
## Problem
Redundant code.

## Solution
- path_has_drive_letter() is now Windows-only and only checks "X:". Other variants and the following-separator requirement are dropped, since they are only relevant when parsing paths with a file scheme prefix. Currently callers only need to distinguish "X:" prefix from a url.
- Rename path_is_url() to path_like_url().
- path_with_url() stops treating "X:" as a drive letter on Unix, so single-letter schemes (e.g. "c:/foo") are recognized as urls there.
- Rework file_name_in_line() to track ":" while scanning backwards, so gf/<cfile> picks the right start for filepath/url.

<!--
  Thank you for contributing to Neovim!
  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

comment_data.body:
```c
return p[0] == ':' && vim_ispathsep_nocolon(p[1]);
```

`xdg-open` supports `http:/`, `http://`, `http:\` and `http:\\` (ubuntu 24.04, firefox)
`open` supports `http:/`, `http://`, `http:\`, but not `http:\\` (mac, firefox/chrome)
Not sure if this change meets the goal.

I would not expect `\` slashes in urls to ever reach here. If e.g. `vim.ui.open` or `gx` or `gf` ... wants to support `http:\\`, it should covert the slashes first.

This low-level C code should not try to support `\` slashes in URLs at all.

"Is this really needed on Unix?" is the wrong question. It usually *simplifies* our life if we have one way of doing things.

We don't need to support single-letter schemes.

If `:\\` isn't common, perhaps we could just drop it?
As for `gf`, I did the conversion after extracting the path. At the time, I had some considerations:
* It shares `file_name_at_cursor` with `<cfile>`, and I assumed `<cfile>` should return the original text.
* Although I did some digging, I wasn't sure whether it would be straightforward enough to normalize separators before matching.

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d1b811b6c2d93fe13442d61331a9276fea417f7b/src/nvim/file_search.c#L1611-L1615

Also, I recently noticed [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/38915#issuecomment-4247494868). Does this mean that `gf`'s logic could move to lua? If so, perhaps conversion could be done there. BTW, I noticed that `gx` can fall back to `<cfile>`, not sure whether the new `gf` implementation would do the same.

This TODO was mainly about using `ASCII_ISALPHA(p[0]) && p[1] == ':'` here, so Unix would also treat `x:/` as a file path (`path_has_drive_letter` always returns false on Unix for now).

As for scheme support, I actually considered using `BufReadCmd` patterns to register schemes and querying them here, with `://` as a fallback. This idea came to me while looking at the [earlier attempt](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/19797) to change `://` to `:/` for deno's `deno:/` scheme, to better  align with the URI syntax. I'm not sure whether this is worth digging into further, though, so just left it in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39592#discussion_r3838811869. :D

> If `:\\` isn't common, perhaps we could just drop it?

drop it where? my previous comment was intended to say that yes, we should not handle `:\\` explicitly here in this C code. the "boundaries" should covert the slashes before `:\\` ever reaches this.



> and I assumed `<cfile>` should return the original text

idk. if it simplifies things then we can just document that it returns the normalized form. that should probably be its own PR though, to help with revert/bisect.



> recently noticed [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/38915#issuecomment-4247494868). Does this mean that `gf`'s logic could move to lua?

yes, my assumption is that `gf` has no reason to live in C.

> BTW, I noticed that `gx` can fall back to `<cfile>`, not sure whether the new `gf` implementation would do the same.

i would assume so. but actually it might make sense for `<cfile>` parsing to live in Lua...

> I actually considered using `BufReadCmd` patterns to register schemes

you mean like what [netrw does](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/510f61555b9da5800ccd13de2336c90a64c0b9a5/runtime/pack/dist/opt/netrw/plugin/netrwPlugin.vim#L41-L44) ?

Not quite. What I had in mind was adding some logic to `autocmd_register`(maybe) and `path_with_url`: the former would mark valid patterns from sth like `:autocmd BufReadCmd urn:*` as supported uri schemes, and the latter could query that information to recognize `urn:isbn:9780307476463` as a uri and skip the path concatenation in `fix_fname`.
I feel this would allow users/lsp clients to support whatever uri formats they need, without requiring at least `:/` or `://` as we do currently.
I don't really get why a registry is needed. All URIs should be supported. Anyway, is this a blocking question, or something we can track as an issue to figure out the shape?

Definitely not a blocker for our cleanup PR. We can always discuss it separately in other issues. I only came up with this while looking into `path_with_url` and `fix_fname`: after going through #19797, #19967, and #39592, I realized that the current uri support may not be sufficient for lsp client in core. :)
